title: Decouple provisioning workflows and simplify node lifecycle interfaces
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Background: Over the last 18 months the capacity planner and node provisioning code paths have accreted features and side-effects: leasepool semantics, implicit DB migrations, node state machine logic mixed with cloud provider calls, and autoscaler retry heuristics. This ticket aims to reduce cognitive complexity by carving a clear boundary between: (1) the capacity planner (decisioning: how many and what type of nodes we need) and (2) the provisioning worker (actuation: create/update/delete nodes). The goal is to make lifecycle transitions explicit, remove in-line cloud provider retries from the planner, and introduce a compact interface for node lifecycle hooks so future features (spot handling, preemptible pooling, upgrade draining) can be implemented without touching planner logic.
acceptance_criteria: CapacityPlanner no longer calls cloud provider APIs directly; instead emits intent objects consumed by Provisioner
Node lifecycle state transitions move to lifecycle service with deterministic retry/backoff policy
End-to-end e2e tests cover scale-up, scale-down, and node termination scenarios with simulated cloud failures
Autoscaler unit tests updated and flakiness reduced (CI pass rate >= 98% for autoscaler suite)
Benchmark: 10% lower median decision latency for CapacityPlanner under 99th-percentile load (measured on staging)
No user-facing capacity loss during canary rollout on dedicated pools (follow rollout checklist)
implementation_steps: 1. Add a small 'ProvisionIntent' proto and DB table to record desired node actions (create/update/delete)
2. Introduce Provisioner service that polls ProvisionIntent and performs cloud provider calls with centralized retry/backoff
3. Refactor CapacityPlanner to emit ProvisionIntent instead of calling Provider APIs; add transactional visibility to intents
4. Extract node-state-machine into lifecycle package with well-documented transitions and side-effect hooks
5. Update autoscaler reconcile loop to react to intent status rather than raw cloud responses
6. Create migration plan and backward-compatibility shim for running planner and provisioner concurrently during rollout
7. Add integration tests and run canary against a subset of dedicated pools
8. Monitor key SLOs (offer latency, provisioning latency, failed create rate) and iterate
tech_notes: Trade-offs: Adding ProvisionIntent increases write amplification and introduces eventual consistency between planner decision and cloud state. We mitigate via quick-path sync for small pools and strict transactional fencing. We considered a full event-sourcing rewrite but scoped work to an intent-based pattern to minimize risk. This refactor will enable future optimizations: batching cloud calls, better retry heuristics, and clear audit trails for provisioning decisions.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Intent table lag can cause duplicate creates or transient over-provisioning. Mitigation: Use idempotent create with provider idempotency tokens and an intent deduplication window. Risk: Migration complexity. Mitigation: run planner v2 in 'emit-only' mode with provisioner shim, validate metrics in staging for 2 weeks before cutover.

notes_for_rollout: Will roll out in three phases: (A) Deploy provisioner in read-only passthrough mode to collect metrics, (B) Enable provisioner for a single dedicated pool (canary) for 72 hours, (C) Gradual ramp to 100% with rollback guard rails. During canary enable transparent logging to Slack #gpu-ops and create a one-click rollback playbook.
postmortem_plan: If we observe provisioning regressions > 1% failed create or > 30m median provisioning latency increase, trigger incident playbook, revert to previous planner behavior, and perform a postmortem within 5 business days. Document findings in /incidents and link back to this ticket.
